title: Burning During Urination
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a 19-year-old sexually active man who presents with dysuria, fevers, and chills. Rectal exam reveals an edematous, tender prostate — the key finding that localizes the infection to the prostate rather than the bladder or urethra alone. He denies flank pain or CVA tenderness (making pyelonephritis less likely). The differential includes cystitis, urethritis, pyelonephritis, and sexually transmitted infections (Chlamydia, gonorrhea). E. coli accounts for approximately one-third of prostatitis cases. Fluoroquinolones are the treatment of choice due to their ability to penetrate the inflamed prostate.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Determine how sick the patient looks.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: Investigate for lung pathology.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Investigate for cardiac pathology.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Abdomen
stacks.finding: Urinary problems could be caused by abdominal pathology.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Genitalia
stacks.finding: Chief complaint — genital exam essential.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Rectal
stacks.finding: Edematous, tender prostate on DRE — key finding that localizes infection to prostate.

stacks.label: Urinalysis
stacks.finding: Quick diagnostic tool. Shows pyuria, bacteriuria.

stacks.label: Gram stain, urine, unspun
stacks.finding: Guides antibiotic treatment by identifying organism class (gram-negative rods = E. coli).

stacks.label: Chlamydia testing (DNA probe / DFA / culture)
stacks.finding: In any suspected prostatitis, rule out STIs — Chlamydia must be excluded.

stacks.label: Gonorrhea testing (DNA probe / culture)
stacks.finding: In any suspected urethritis/prostatitis, rule out gonorrhea.

stacks.label: Bacterial culture, urine
stacks.finding: Before antibiotic treatment, always get urine culture. Confirms organism and sensitivities.

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: CBC important in febrile patient. Leukocytosis expected.

stacks.label: Pulse oximetry
stacks.finding: In any febrile patient, know oxygenation status.

stacks.label: Basic metabolic profile / Comprehensive metabolic profile
stacks.finding: BMPs are excellent screening tools.

stacks.label: Ciprofloxacin / TMP-SMX / Levofloxacin
stacks.finding: Fluoroquinolones are first-line for prostatitis — excellent penetration of inflamed prostate. TMP-SMX is alternative. Treat 14-28 days for chronic bacterial prostatitis.

stacks.label: Advise patient, drive with seat belt
stacks.finding: Emphasize seat belt use — common cause of death in young adults.

stacks.label: Advise patient, safe sex techniques
stacks.finding: Patient has history of risky sexual practices — review safe sex to prevent future STIs.

stacks.label: Reassure patient
stacks.finding: Reassuring the patient is good medicine.

stacks.label: Tdap vaccine
stacks.finding: Tdap every 10 years. No history given — should be administered.

stacks.label: Meningococcal vaccine
stacks.finding: College-age patient should receive meningitis vaccine.

physical_exam.abdominal: Suprapubic tenderness may be present. No CVA tenderness (rules out pyelonephritis).
physical_exam.genitourinary: Dysuria. Urethral discharge absent. Testicular exam normal.
physical_exam.rectal: Edematous, tender prostate on digital rectal exam — pathognomonic for prostatitis. CAUTION: do not perform vigorous prostate massage — risk of bacteremia.

decoys.label: Blood culture
decoys.reason_wrong: Patient does not meet SIRS criteria. Blood cultures not necessary for uncomplicated prostatitis without sepsis.

decoys.label: Vigorous prostate massage
decoys.reason_wrong: Can cause bacteremia. Gentle DRE is sufficient for diagnosis.

decoys.label: Ceftriaxone as sole therapy
decoys.reason_wrong: Ceftriaxone does not adequately penetrate the prostate. Fluoroquinolones are the treatment of choice.

teach_me_steps.order: Digital rectal exam for prostate assessment
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Tender, edematous prostate localizes infection. DRE differentiates prostatitis from cystitis and urethritis.

teach_me_steps.order: Urine culture + STI testing BEFORE antibiotics
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Urine culture and gram stain identify the organism. Test for Chlamydia and gonorrhea in sexually active patients.
Ciprofloxacin penetrates inflamed prostate better than other antibiotics. TMP-SMX is alternative. E. coli = ~1/3 of cases.
Uncomplicated prostatitis in stable patient can be managed as outpatient. Hospitalize only if septic or unable to tolerate PO.

case_summary: Acute bacterial prostatitis in sexually active 19-year-old. DRE: tender, edematous prostate. Urine gram stain: gram-negative rods (E. coli). UA + urine culture + STI panel + CBC → ciprofloxacin 14-28 days. Office management. Prevention: Tdap, meningococcal vaccine, safe sex counseling.
